blocks.text: A transgenic animal carries a foreign gene to produce the desired protein. Transgenic animals serve various purposes e.g., producing drugs, enhancing yields, increasing resistance to disease etc. For example;

blocks.title: Tidbit
blocks.text: In theory, foreign genes may be inserted either in germline or in somatic cells of humans. If genes are inserted in germline cells, it results in inheritable changes. But, most research has focused on somatic cells because of risks and ethical issues associated with germline transformation.

items: Transgenic dairy cows have genes from human beings to produce milk that is the same as human breast milk.

blocks.title: Tidbit
blocks.text: Since the mid-1980s, transgenic mice are a key model for investigating diseases. Mice are the model for this purpose because there is complete analysis of its genome sequence and its genome is very much similar to humans.

blocks.alt: Three white mice on a dark background. The left and right mice glow blue under light, with bright green eyes, nose, ears and paws, and glowing green tails; each is labelled 'Transgenic'. The middle mouse is plain white with a dark eye and is labelled 'Normal'. Green text at the top reads: Transgenic mice carry a gene of protein which glows green.

items: Transgenic goats produce milk with strong spiderweb-like silk proteins.
Transgenic goats also produce human enzyme lysozyme in their milk to fight diarrhoea causing bacteria in humans.
Transgenic fish show better growth, reduced food intake, increased cold tolerance, and disease resistance.
In gene therapy, genetically modified viruses are used to deliver genes to humans to cure various inheritable diseases such as abnormal development of T and B cells and inherited blindness.
The first human biological drug produced from a transgenic goat was an anticoagulant to reduce the probability of blood clots during surgery or childbirth.
Malaria-resistant mosquitoes have been developed in the laboratory by inserting a gene that reduces the development of Plasmodium in them.
